session.question: In the manufacturing firms study, how did SS relate to sustainability audits, and how is that different from the Metaverse study where SS had no significant impact on student perceptions?
session.answer:
In the manufacturing firms study, sustainability sensitivity (SS) showed a significant positive relationship with sustainability audits. This means that higher SS was associated with more extensive or more effective sustainability auditing within the firms, alongside positive links reported for internal audit effectiveness and risk management processes. (amoako2023internalauditfunctions chunk 1)

This differs from the Metaverse study in two key ways. First, there SS referred to social sustainability as the dependent outcome being predicted by the model, not a predictor of another organizational process. Second, the study reported that students’ perceptions of Metaverse technology were significantly influenced by performance expectancy, facilitating conditions, and extraversion, while effort expectancy and social influence were not significant; it did not report SS as having a significant impact on student perceptions. (alkhwaldi2024investigatingthesocial chunk 1)

Accordingly, the manufacturing study treated SS as an explanatory factor positively associated with sustainability audits, whereas the Metaverse study treated SS as the outcome and did not identify SS as a significant driver of perceptions. (amoako2023internalauditfunctions chunk 1, alkhwaldi2024investigatingthesocial chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-188dcbd9: The study examined four internal audit functions and their relationship with sustainability audits in manufacturing firms. One of the functions was sustainability sensitivity (SS). The results showed that sustainability sensitivity had a significant positive relationship with sustainability audits, meaning higher SS was associated with better or more extensive sustainability auditing. The paper also noted that internal audit effectiveness and risk management processes were positively related to sustainability audits.
From Gilbert K. Amoako, Jonas Bawuah, Emmanuel Asafo‐Adjei, and Catherine Ayimbire. Internal audit functions and sustainability audits: insights from manufacturing firms. Cogent Business & Management, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1080/23311975.2023.2192313, doi:10.1080/23311975.2023.2192313.

pqac-19780965: The study examined factors affecting students’ perceptions toward the social sustainability (SS) of Metaverse technology in Jordanian higher education. It used UTAUT factors plus perceived curiosity and extraversion. The results showed that students’ perceptions toward Metaverse were significantly influenced by performance expectancy, facilitating conditions, and extraversion. However, effort expectancy and social influence had no significant impact on SS. The excerpt does not indicate that SS itself affected student perceptions; rather, SS was the outcome being explained by the model.
From Abeer F. Alkhwaldi. Investigating the social sustainability of immersive virtual technologies in higher educational institutions: students’ perceptions toward metaverse technology. Sustainability, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su16020934, doi:10.3390/su16020934.

pqac-5717eca3: The excerpt describes a 2024 study on manufacturing firms that examined the relationships among HRM, Occupational Health and Safety (OHS), and Sustainability Organizational Outcomes (SOO) using survey data from 256 employees at Balexco in Bahrain and Structural Equation Modeling. The abstract reports significant positive relationships between HRM, SOO, and OHS, and notes that OHS mediated the effect of HRM on SOO. However, the excerpt does not mention “SS” or sustainability audits, so no direct relationship between SS and sustainability audits is provided here.
From Ali Ateeq, Abd Al-Aziz Al-Refaei, Mohammed Alzoraiki, Marwan Milhem, Ali Nasser Al-Tahitah, and Abdulhadi Ibrahim. Sustaining organizational outcomes in manufacturing firms: the role of hrm and occupational health and safety. Sustainability, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su16031035, doi:10.3390/su16031035.

pqac-004d0ffe: The excerpt describes a 2021 empirical study on Industry 4.0 implementation and triple bottom line sustainability in Malaysian small and medium manufacturing firms. It focuses on determinants such as top management commitment, supply chain integration, and IT infrastructure, and reports that top management and IT infrastructure significantly affect Industry 4.0 implementation and sustainability, while supply chain integration is insignificant. The excerpt does not mention “SS” or sustainability audits, so it provides no direct information about any relationship between SS and sustainability audits.
From Sreenivasan Jayashree, Mohammad Nurul Hassan Reza, C. A. Malarvizhi, and Muhammad Mohiuddin. Industry 4.0 implementation and triple bottom line sustainability: an empirical study on small and medium manufacturing firms. Heliyon, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heliyon.2021.e07753, doi:10.1016/j.heliyon.2021.e07753.

pqac-61f88e6e: The excerpt describes a systematic literature review on using Metaverse-based virtual educational spaces during COVID-19. It reports generally positive student perceptions: students mostly enjoyed learning with Metaverse and often understood lessons better than with traditional textbook or face-to-face methods. The paper also notes that teacher and parent guidance is still needed to avoid disadvantages. However, this excerpt does not mention “SS” or provide any specific statistical result about SS affecting student perceptions, nor whether that effect was significant.
From Cindy Amanda Onggirawan, Jocelyn Michelle Kho, Arya Putra Kartiwa, Anderies, and Alexander A S Gunawan. Systematic literature review: the adaptation of distance learning process during the covid-19 pandemic using virtual educational spaces in metaverse. Procedia Computer Science, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.procs.2022.12.137, doi:10.1016/j.procs.2022.12.137.
